margin_framing.metric_basis_note: No long-term margin level target has been given. Numeric framing is (1) a $100M run-rate cost savings plan by end of fiscal 2026, already exceeded, and (2) one-year guides: fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA $475M to $525M on revenue $2.3B to $2.4B (21.3% at the midpoints) and total gross margin about 54% (+140 bps). Fiscal year ends June; Baba FY labels match Peloton fiscal years (FY2027 = July 2026 to June 2027).

statements.quote: Our fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $400 million-$450 million reflects an increase of $21 million, or 5% year-over-year at the midpoint, primarily driven by operating expense savings connected to the new restructuring plan we introduced today. We've actioned roughly half of the run rate cost savings as of today and expect the remainder to be realized over the course of the year. Roughly 15% of the $100 million run rate savings goal is expected to come from lower stock-based compensation.

street.gap_assumption: Target is the fiscal 2027 guide midpoint ($500M EBITDA on $2.35B revenue = 21.28%) versus FY2027 consensus 21.13%: +15 bps (data_compute). FY2026 is actual ($468.2M on $2,445.9M). Consensus is flat after FY2027: 21.51% FY2028, 21.16% FY2031. The $100M savings target is already delivered and in the base.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q3 fiscal 2026, Q4 fiscal 2026], adj. EBITDA / revenue. Q3 20.0% ($126.2M on $630.9M) vs 14.3% ($89.3M on $624.0M), VA actuals. Q4 23.4% ($142M on $608M, CFO, document_id 130364) vs 23.1%; excluding the $24M patent-litigation accrual Q4 was 27.3%, about +423 bps. Fiscal 2026 was the first full year of positive operating income ($161M) and net income ($63M).

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus. The dated $100M savings target is delivered and in the base, and FY2027 consensus (21.13%) sits 15 bps under the guide midpoint. CEO Stern (2025-01-01) is outside the 18-month window; the in-window catalyst is a new external CFO (2026-06-22) with no promised framework event.
verdict: Cheap and down 53%, with a new external CFO and COO, but there is no multi-year margin target and the street already sits on the FY2027 guide, so the GXO-type gap is missing.
open_questions: Will Thacker set a multi-year margin or EBITDA framework with the refinancing or an investor event?
Revenue is guided down 3.9% for FY2027 and consensus is flat through FY2031: is the setup a revenue question rather than a margin one?
How much of the FY2027 EBITDA growth is the non-recurring $24M legal accrual rolling off versus real cost leverage?
